issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers class defines a method named appendElement (ArrayHelpers.appendElement), but other template classes (e.g., Stock.java) call ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray. This name/signature mismatch between the method definition and its usages causes a compile-time error and will prevent students from building and running the project. The solution repository uses addElementToArray (the name expected by Stock.java), indicating the template's appendElement name is accidental and inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers to match the usages in the template (and solution): change appendElement to addElementToArray, keeping the same signature and behavior. Alternatively, update all usages (e.g., in Stock.java) to call appendElement. Ensuring consistent method names across ArrayHelpers and its callers will allow the project to compile and align the template with the solution.

issues.description: The ArrayHelpers utility method used by Stock is named addElementToArray in code that consumes it, but the template implementation of ArrayHelpers defines the method as appendElement. The solution repository uses addElementToArray. This naming mismatch in the template (between the method definition and its use) will prevent students from mapping the documented helper usage to the template code and causes a compile/runtime issue. It creates unnecessary cognitive load and blocks straightforward development.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ArrayHelpers API consistent across artifacts. Rename the template method appendElement to addElementToArray (matching Stock.java and the solution), or change the Stock.java usage to call appendElement. Preferably update the template ArrayHelpers to provide addElementToArray with the same signature (or add a forwarding method) so the helper name matches both the template usage and the solution.
